big_picture:
All four reps agree on the most important point, and the code confirms it. Part 1's content is an honest, unaided check: every typed task is checked with other values. The site's testout wiring is what makes Unit 10 dishonest. Three things combine:
- UnitPage.tsx takes every testout out of the item list.
- nextUpItem then sends students from the intro straight to the mini-boss.
- LessonPlayer.tsx:119 calls markTestedOut when any form passes, including the 9-minute rc-recheck. That marks the mini-boss and rc-explain tested out without anyone holding the ward.

The fix is site work, and it needs no new content field. rc-part1-a is the only testout in the course with optional=False, so the site can treat a required testout as a core item with no unit test-out (site request 1).

On the content side, three themes:
1. **A student who misses something can find the way back.** rc-review moves right after Part 1 A, each line is labelled by the task titles students actually saw, a "Start here" lesson is marked, the twin tasks are named, and the intro and summary point to it.
2. **Remove traps that test our wiring, not their skill.** Form B's `ward` now means the same as in form A (`ward_name` for the name; the page stays `page`). The mini-boss comment numbers are explained as check order. The CP1/CP3 hint ladders teach the move under `else:` early, with a picture that uses other names. Form A's starter for the function-from-its-goal task gets the same numbered comments as B and C, and "Stuck? Skip it" now appears in every form.
3. **Name the slip in words the class reads correctly.** Messages now say "typed", explain None as "Python's word for nothing", say "holds a typed 24" instead of "stayed 24", and give mini-boss evidence in short sentences with no parentheses inside parentheses.

For honest learning:
- rc-explain moves to the pay line, the class-wide combine-values gap, with choices of similar length.
- Form A's ledger question becomes typed.
- The questions come first, so the first win is a prediction.
- Compare opens after 5 minutes only, as the intro already promises. A pass after Compare is recorded and points the student to mini-boss B.
- Quiz retakes draw another form's questions.

For ready-to-stretch students there is a new optional, advanced, goal-only trial. Mini-boss B stays dictated, because it is the follow-up for students who needed Mar'tu's version.

Core time stays about 46 minutes (2 + 10 + 18 + 15 + 1), inside the ~60-minute budget. rc-review (15) and the trial are optional. The campaign link stays "you've seen this, now you'll get it".

site_requests: Readiness flow, the MUST from all four reps. A unit that holds a required testout (`kind: 'testout'` with `optional: false`; today only rc-part1-a) gets: (1) No Quick Check offer box. Its testouts and their `-questions` quizzes are listed in 'Lessons and more' in ITEMS order (questions first for Part 1 A), and rc-part1-a and its questions are core rows. (2) Never call markTestedOut for that unit (LessonPlayer.tsx:119), and itemStatus never shows 'tested-out' there; the mini-boss and rc-explain must be done by the student, and Ready (5.5) needs the mini-boss. (3) The optional forms rc-part1-b and rc-part1-c, and their questions, show as locked rows ('Opens after Part 1 A and Mar'tu's notes') until Part 1 A was tried (every task attempted and the questions answered once) and rc-review was opened. (4) rc-recheck and its questions stay hidden until the unit's core is done and about 7 days have passed, or the teacher unlocks them. (5) nextUpItem follows this list: intro, questions, tasks, mini-boss, explain. After Part 1 A, Continue goes to rc-review only when something was missed, otherwise to the mini-boss. Earlier units' optional Quick Checks keep today's behavior.

Questions gate retake: in the readiness unit, a failed questions quiz's retake serves the next form's questions (A, then B, then C) instead of the same 12 reshuffled. That score counts toward the required form's questions_to_pass. Show a question's explain/why_wrong once, never on the same question again.

Per-item Readiness scoring with twins: an item missed in form A counts as passed when its twin task or question in form B or C passes (rc-review names the twins), so a student redoes one task, not a whole form. Show the Ready / Ready with a review list / Review first result, with links to the missed items' lessons.

Explainer rule, string indices: `TypeError: string indices must be integers, not 'str'` (`ward_name["effect"](hero)`, or in form B the old habit) gets a new lean kind, 'text read like a sheet'. As evidence it names the variable on that line ('`ward_name` holds text, not a sheet').

Explainer rule, borrowed names: a NameError for a campaign name (`party`, `move_left`, `caster`, `spell`, `spell_name`, `print_prompt`, `cast_spell`) or for the other mini-boss form's name (`ward` in use_ward, `caster`/`page` in cast_ward) gets a lean kind, 'a name from the campaign, not this program'. Its evidence lists the enclosing function's own parameters and variables. Also hide Python's 'Did you mean: …' on the shown last line when it suggests a name this student never met ('aiter' for `caster`).

Explainer rule, unquoted key: a NameError on a name that sits inside `[ ]` as a dictionary key (`mana = hero[mana]`) fires the unquoted-word rule even on the line that makes that same name. Lean name: 'a key with no quotes'.

Explainer rule, library frames: when the error is raised inside a library frame (random.py, e.g. `random.randint(1, "die_size")` giving 'can only concatenate str (not "int") to str'), point at the student's main.py line and never at random.py. When that call passes a string equal to a parameter or variable name, name 'a parameter's name in quotes'. This covers roll-the-die, throw-the-die and toss-the-die.
